The AJ system is compatible with a wide range of inks, pastes, or other materials including metals, conductors, insulators, ferrites, and polymers. It can also be used for direct-write biologics processes to deposit cells, enzymes, proteins, nucleic acid, and other biological materials. The AJ print system includes a graphical user interface (GUI) to assist in toolpath generation and material printing. The software interface provides complete on-screen motion control, a vision system for process viewing, and various other tools for printing and processing materials. 1.2 HD2 Print System The HD2 print subsystem is designed for low-volume production and research printing environments, with configurations varying based on customer requirements and print application. A basic setup consists of a print head and an ultrasonic and/or pneumatic atomizer. HD2 ultrasonic atomizer cassette The HD2 ultrasonic atomizer cassette uses an ultrasonic transducer to atomize the liquid source material. The transducer creates high-frequency pressure waves within the coupling fluid reservoir. These pressure waves are transmitted through the coupling fluid (typically water) into the atomizer vial, causing the ink or other liquid source material to atomize into small droplets. The atomized droplets are then entrained in a gas stream and delivered to the deposition print head. The ultrasonic atomizer is best suited for materials with a viscosity of approximately 1 to 10 cP. Inks and materials with high vapor pressures can be used. Particulate suspensions may also be atomized, but there is a limit to the particle size that can be contained in an ejected droplet. Generally, suspended particles should be 50 nm or less. New materials require case-by-case testing. HD2 pneumatic atomizer cassette The HD2 pneumatic atomizer uses a high-velocity gas stream to shear a liquid into small droplets, typically 1 to 5 µm in diameter. Compressed gas expands through the atomizer nozzle, creating a high-velocity jet that draws ink from the reservoir and breaks

HD2 pneumatic atomizer cassette The HD2 pneumatic atomizer uses a high-velocity gas stream to shear a liquid into small droplets, typically 1 to 5 µm in diameter. Compressed gas expands through the atomizer nozzle, creating a high-velocity jet that draws ink from the reservoir and breaks the liquid stream into droplets. Large droplets impact the sidewalls of the atomizer reservoir and drain back into it, while smaller particles remain suspended in the gas. The gas flow rates required for the high-velocity jet are too high for direct use with the AJ deposition head. To address this, a virtual impactor concentrates the aerosol stream by removing excess atomization gas, preventing material loss. The output from the virtual impactor is then directed to the print head. The pneumatic atomizer can be used for inks, pastes, or other materials with a viscosity range of approximately 1 to 1000 cP. Particulate suspensions can be atomized, generally with suspended particles less than 500 nm in size. Solvents with low to medium vapor pressure are suitable for this system; however, high vapor pressure solvents might lead to excessive drying and produce powdery or porous deposits. HD2 Print Head The print head is capable of printing features as small as 10 µm onto almost any surface. The aerosol stream generated by either atomizer type is fed into the print head, where it is surrounded by a sheath gas stream that focuses and accelerates the aerosol stream, causing it to impact the target workpiece. This sheath stream effect is commonly known as aerodynamic focusing. A motorized platen moves the workpiece beneath the nozzle, allowing deposited material to be sprayed onto it. A process divert is employed to interrupt the flow of the focused aerosol stream, pausing or stopping the printing process. The nozzles for the deposition head are interchangeable. Fine feature nozzles are available in sizes ranging from 100 µm to 300 µm. Wide feature nozzles are available with circular cross-section diameters of 635 µm and 1 mm. It controls the AJ hardware through the knowledge engineered workstation application, or KEWA™, which comprises a suite of graphical user interfaces (GUIs). These GUIs provide comprehensive on-screen motion control, a vision system for alignment and process viewing, and various other tools for material printing and processing. Incorporating this feature requires the installation of all appropriate safety options, including safety switches and laser-safe glass on the enclosure. 1.3.3 Light Bar Ultraviolet Cure and Deposition Lighting Module (optional) The Mightex light controller manages the visible light LEDs for deposition lighting and the 365 nm ultraviolet (UV) LEDs for curing. The UV cure module can be used for in-situ curing of printed material with ultraviolet light. This UV light allows deposited materials to be cured directly without damaging the underlying substrate, even for materials printed onto low-temperature workpieces. Included with the light bars is a film designed to prevent printed material from re-depositing or curing onto the UV LED lens. If a noticeable decrease in light intensity occurs, these components may need replacement.
